messages.subject: Understanding how areas-allowed affects models with j parameter
messages.subject_clean: Understanding how areas-allowed affects models with j parameter
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have been running the 'out of the box' approach, and had a question about how disallowing areas affects the j parameter (if it does). I am trying to constrain the biogeographic estimations to adjacent areas, and so constrained the state space, as found on the biogeobears tutorials. However, in the models that add in the j parameter, the areas are allowed to transition directly between non-adjacent areas.

E.g.:
A <-> B <-> C = not allowing AC, but seeing a transition in my trees of A->C

I understand that the founder-event speciation events could look like this, and that classic examples do exactly this. However, since I am studying aquatic organisms in adjacent freshwater systems, I want to ensure I am considering the implications (or unlikely nature) of passing directly through a system without range expansion. Presumably, if long-distance dispersal is allowed, the j-parameter should allow skipping several adjacent areas as well (if this scenario is most likely). If simulating adjacent areas is only intended for the models without the j parameter, then I believe the code is running correctly.

Thank you,
Tom

messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] Understanding how areas-allowed affects models with j parameter
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom, from what you describe, it seems the model is running correctly. The "areas allowed" option will only affect anagenetic dispersal (modeled with the parameter d) in this case -- species cannot disperse from A to C forming the range AC. But cladogenetic dispersal (modeled with j) is always the dispersal from a previous range to a single new area, so A > C is allowed because it does not go through the prohibited range AC.

You can probably disallow A > C by editing the distance matrix or manual dispersal multipliers, and setting dispersal between these areas to 0 -- but I am not sure if this affects both d and j, or only d.

Hope this helps!
Best,
Ivan
